set.approach: Start at the Molas Pass (Elk Park) trailhead on US 550, about five miles south of Silverton. Follow the Colorado Trail down to the Animas River crossing, then turn up the Elk Creek trail for roughly three and a half miles to the beaver ponds, just under 10,000 feet. The spire's west buttress is the obvious line seen from the ponds. Continue on the rougher, unmaintained trail into the Vestal Creek drainage (fallen logs and avalanche chutes) toward the 11,760-foot camps, about nine miles and 2,900 feet from the car, then work around to the west side toward the Arrow-Electric saddle and find the ramp that climbs south to the base.
set.descent_text: From the summit towers the usual way off is back into the notch and down the loose gully below it. Downclimb most of the gully and make a rappel of about 150 feet at the bottom, where older anchors may still be in place. Test or back up any old hardware, and keep a rope and some slings in the pack.
hazards: Afternoon thunderstorms on the exposed towers; start early and be off the top by midday
Very loose gully on the descent below the notch
Runout climbing on the second pitch, with overhangs
Exposed moves around the towers just below the summit

review.notes: summitpost page returned 403 on direct fetch; its content was seen via the Mountain Project page which carries the same text. Distance and gain skipped: no page states them for the spire itself (the 9 mi / 2,900 ft figure is only to the Vestal camp, stated in prose). Season skipped, no page states one. Approach to the spire base from camp is a single-source paraphrase; the Arrow Peak page does not mention the spire.

set.approach: Start at the Molas Pass (Elk Park) trailhead on US 550, about five miles south of Silverton. Follow the Colorado Trail to the Animas River crossing, take the Elk Creek trail past the beaver ponds, then an unmaintained trail with fallen logs and avalanche chutes up Vestal Creek to the camps near 11,760 feet, about nine miles and 2,900 feet from the car. From there the climb goes over West Trinity, then descends its east ridge to the saddle where the west ridge starts.
hazards: Loose boulder talus and rubble throughout; rockfall onto anyone below
Short exposed chimney and fourth-class section where a fall would be serious
Early-season snow on the approach to the Vestal-Trinity saddle; an ice axe is advised
Unmaintained Vestal Creek trail with deadfall and avalanche debris
set.overview: The west ridge is the Class 4 link between West Trinity and Trinity Peak, deep in the Grenadier Range. From the saddle east of West Trinity the line stays below the south-side cliffs on cairned ledges, passes a short, exposed chimney of about twenty feet, then a brief fourth-class step to the crest and an easy walk on solid rock to the summit. The terrain is loose boulders and rubble, and it is a serious objective for experienced scramblers.

review.notes: Gain and distance skipped: the only published figures (22.75 mi / 7,150 ft round trip, 4.75 mi / 4,250 ft from camp) include West Trinity, a second summit. Descent skipped: the page gives none for Trinity (people usually continue to the other Trinities). Season skipped: not stated.

set.approach: The usual start is the Burns Gulch trailhead at 10,790 feet, reached by driving east from Silverton on County Road 2 along the Animas River. The final road is a rough shelf road that is best with high clearance. A river ford on the way depends on water level. Driving the upper road saves about two miles of walking each way and over 900 feet of gain compared with parking low.
hazards: Unstable talus, loose scree and dirt slow progress along the ridge
Steep drop on the north side of Jones; stay on the south side of the crest
Easy to wander onto the southeast ridge in poor visibility
Animas River ford and narrow single-lane shelf road on the way to the trailhead
set.overview: A Class 2 ridge walk to Niagara Peak, normally the third summit after American Peak and Jones Mountain. From the Jones saddle the route drops about 640 feet, then regains roughly 600 feet on talus and scree to the top. Keep to the south side of the ridge to stay clear of Jones's steep north face, and stay on the main ridge rather than drifting onto the southeast ridge in poor visibility.

review.notes: Gain and distance skipped: published figures (9.6 mi / 4,145 ft) cover American, Jones and Niagara together; Jones-to-Niagara alone is 0.9 mi / 590 ft, not a trailhead figure. Descent skipped: page gives none (implied retrace). Season skipped: not stated. Only one page opened for this route.

set.approach: Park at the climbers' campground on Castle Valley Road, a quarter to half mile past the cattle guard on the left. Walk up the wash, following cairns, to a dirt road, cross it at the cairn and signpost, and follow the signed trail up the steep talus cone to the tower. The hike is roughly a mile and a quarter to a mile and three-quarters with about 1,350 to 1,550 feet of climbing and takes an hour or more. Stay on the trail to protect the soil crust.
hazards: Steep, loose approach trail with short scrambling sections
Wet sandstone is weak: do not climb in or just after rain
Summer heat can pass 100 degrees; carry extra water or climb in the cool months
Spring raptor closures are common in the Moab area; check before going

review.notes: Gain and distance skipped: tower-base approach figures (1.7 mi / 1,549 ft vs 1.25 mi / 1,350 ft) differ by more than 10% and are not a summit figure; desert tower so optional. Season Sep-May is a one-window summary of spring and fall best, winter on sunny aspects possible, summer too hot. Descent not in fill.

set.approach: Park at the climbers' campground on Castle Valley Road and take the Castleton Tower trail up the wash and the steep talus cone. Near the top of the cone, a trail crosses the ridgeline to the base of the Rectory. The Empirical Route is the far-left line on the west face, in the right-facing corner that separates the Rectory from the Nuns. Allow about an hour for the approach, which is strenuous; stay on the trail.
hazards: Third pitch is on rotten Wingate sandstone
Run-out sections carry an R rating
Wet sandstone is weak: do not climb in or just after rain
Summer heat and spring raptor closures in the area

review.notes: Descent skipped: no opened page describes it (a trip report mentioned two-rope raps but was only seen in a search summary). Gain/distance skipped (desert tower, optional, no summit figure).

set.approach: Park at the climbers' campground on Castle Valley Road and take the Castleton Tower trail up the wash and talus cone. Near its top turn left at the short cliff band and continue toward the Rectory, traversing left slightly below the Rectory's base. The Priest is the lone tower at the Rectory's north end. The route starts on a large ledge on the tower's west side. Expect an hour or more of steep walking.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route or the north face. One option uses two 60 m ropes down the climb; the other drops the north-face line (Excommunication) with a single 60 or 70 m rope. Ropes can jam or drag on the chimney pitches, and the summit anchor has needed backup, so carry webbing and spare hardware.
hazards: Long run-outs on the first two chimney pitches, and a real chance of getting stuck in the squeeze
Old, widely spaced and partly missing bolts on the third pitch bolt ladder
Aged webbing on slung chockstones and a summit rappel anchor that needs backing up
Strong wind on the tower; wet sandstone is weak so avoid rain

review.notes: Rappel counts deliberately left out (only one page opened). Gain/distance skipped. Grade on page is 5.11a A0; row says 5.11b (not touched).

hazards: Access road is rarely in good condition and can stop vehicles early
Summit anchors are old; back them up
Wet sandstone is weak: do not climb in or just after rain
Spring raptor closures and summer heat in the Moab area

review.notes: No page gives an approach specific to Unknown Sister; the approach is the group's (to Sister Superior). Descent is inferred from summit bolts plus a first-ascent photo caption of rappelling the south side. Gain/distance skipped.

set.approach: Drive about 7 miles east of Moab on River Road and park at a small pullout on the river side, just past a large boulder with calcite on one side. Walk back toward Moab on the road to a trail marked by a metal post; the walk takes about 20 minutes to the west face. The route is on the east side, so first climb a short 5.7 approach pitch up a loose corner to an anchor in the notch on the south side, then walk along the base of the northeast face to the chalked chimney.
set.descent_text: No anchors exist on the summit, so reverse the mantle onto the summit block and downclimb to the fixed anchors. Then either rappel the route with two ropes, walk to the approach-pitch anchors and rappel to your packs, or use a single 70 m rope down the northeast side, a short rappel to a ledge and a long one to the back of the spire.
hazards: Approach pitch is run-out and loose
No summit anchor; the overhanging summit block must be mantled and reversed
Wet sandstone is weak: do not climb in or just after rain
Heat in summer and spring raptor closures

review.notes: Gain/distance skipped. Rappel counts left out.

set.approach: Park at the end of the Fisher Towers road and walk the well-marked main trail for about a mile, past the tower. Turn left onto a climber's trail and follow it, watching for cairns, up the gully between Ancient Art and Cottontail Tower to the base. The route starts with the same approach as Stolen Chimney, then walks about 200 feet right to a sandy slope.
set.descent_text: Walk back to the ledge at the end of the third pitch and rappel twice to a bench. From there either rappel again from a tree or downclimb the start of Stolen Chimney. There are no anchors on the summit itself, so downclimb the final mantle first.
hazards: Last pitch has no fixed protection and ends on a mantle with no summit anchor
Mud-coated, loose Fisher Towers sandstone
Wet sandstone is weak: do not climb in or just after rain
Summer heat and spring raptor closures
set.overview: A four-pitch trad and aid line up the north summit of Ancient Art in the Fisher Towers, sharing its first moves with Stolen Chimney. It follows an arch (5.8), a 5.10+ chimney to a big ledge, a 5.8 offwidth squeeze, and a final unprotected mantle to the top. The sandstone is soft and mud-coated, protection is sparse near the top, and a 70 m rope is suggested.

review.notes: Gain/distance skipped (optional). Season line is the Moab-wide spring/fall summary from a guide page about Castleton, not Fisher Towers specific.

hazards: The summit is a narrow exposed ridge with no anchor on the high point
Mud-coated, loose Fisher Towers sandstone and rockfall from parties above
Wet sandstone is weak: do not climb in or just after rain
Summer heat and spring raptor closures

review.notes: Descent skipped: no page covers it. Approach is generic to Echo Tower; the 40-minute walk comes from a Kingfisher trip report. Gain/distance skipped. Hazards partly area-wide.

hazards: Old or dubious belay bolts; several have pulled
Mud and loose rock on the third and fourth pitches
Long falls are possible on the bolt ladders and at the start of pitch four
Traversing rappels and old fixed gear on the way down; wet sandstone is weak

review.notes: Approach combines the Ancient Art gully description with the route's start location; the exact gully for the north face is not confirmed. 'Shortest approach' line came from a search summary of a summitpost page I could not open; delete if the reviewer objects. Gain/distance skipped.

set.approach: Park at the end of the Fisher Towers road and hike the main trail, roughly 40 minutes to the Kingfisher area. Leave the trail and scramble steeply up loose ground toward the base, passing Ancient Art and the Cobra tower. The route starts about 50 feet right of the line Dead Again.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route. A single-rope rappel reaches the pitch 4 anchors, then double-rope rappels reach the ground. All the bolts have hangers and the pulls are easy.
hazards: Hard aid on the first and second pitches; falls on thin placements are likely
Mud-coated, loose sandstone and rockfall, especially from parties above
Wet sandstone is weak: do not climb in or just after rain
Summer heat and spring raptor closures
set.overview: A five-pitch, 600-foot aid route on the Kingfisher in the Fisher Towers, rated A3 overall. It starts about 50 feet right of Dead Again, climbs a long first pitch of about 170 feet, links thin crack systems with a couple of bolts, then A2 cracks, caprock and a short crack to the summit. It is a nailing-style line best suited to experienced aid climbers.

review.notes: Approach is from a trip report of another Kingfisher route (Northeast Ridge) -- the approach to the tower, not this wall. Gain/distance skipped. Season line is a Moab-wide summary.
